gloss: cherry tree in leaf; cherry tree after blossoms have fallen

definitions.gloss: cherry tree in leaf; cherry tree after blossoms have fallen
definitions.explanation: A cherry tree in the stage when its blossoms have mostly fallen and fresh green leaves have appeared. Evokes the transition from spring's peak to early summer.

examples.japanese: ⟦{桜|さくら}→桜：02212_sakura⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦もう→もう：00602_mou⟧{葉桜|はざくら}になっていた。
examples.english: The cherry trees had already turned to leaf.

examples.japanese: ⟦{花見|はなみ}→花見：01700_hanami⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦シーズン→シーズン：10944_shiizun⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{終|お}わり、⟦{並木|なみき}→並木：00302_namiki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{葉桜|はざくら}になった。
examples.english: The flower-viewing season ended and the tree-lined path turned to leafy cherry trees.

examples.japanese: {葉桜|はざくら}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{下|した}→下：00670_shita⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{散歩|さんぽ}する→散歩する：26840_sanposuru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{花|はな}→花：00523_hana⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{時期|じき}→時期：03269_jiki⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦また→また：00969_mata⟧⟦{違|ちが}った→違う：01957_chigau⟧⟦{静|しず}か→静か：00755_shizuka⟧な{美|うつく}しさ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: When you walk beneath cherry trees in leaf, there is a quiet beauty different from the flowering season.

notes:
USAGE:
{葉桜|はざくら} refers specifically to the stage after the blossoms fall and green leaves emerge. It is a seasonal word (⟦{季語|きご}→季語：09561_kigo⟧) for late spring in haiku.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese culture marks the cherry blossom cycle in fine detail. {葉桜|はざくら} captures the bittersweet moment when the spectacular flowers are gone but the tree enters a fresh, green phase. It is often used poetically to suggest the passing of a beautiful moment.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {葉桜|はざくら}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{季節|きせつ}→季節：01304_kisetsu⟧ (the leafy-cherry season)
- {葉桜|はざくら}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to turn to leaf)
- {葉桜|はざくら}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{並木|なみき}→並木：00302_namiki⟧ (an avenue of leafy cherry trees)
